package_info.package_manager: GitHub (source distribution), Azure VM agent (automatic deployment)
package_info.why_malicious: The OMI agent, as distributed and automatically installed on Azure Linux VMs, contains multiple critical vulnerabilities (OMIGOD) that allow unauthenticated remote code execution and privilege escalation to root. While not intentionally malicious, the presence of these vulnerabilities and the silent, undocumented installation of the agent create a supply-chain risk, enabling attackers to easily compromise affected systems.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (network request to OMI HTTP API)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: if (auth_header == NULL) { execute_request_as_root(); } // CVE-2021-38647: Unauthenticated RCE
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the OMI agent receives an HTTP request on a management port, it checks for the presence of an authentication header; if missing, it processes the request as root, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution by attackers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Processing unauthenticated network requests as root is a critical security vulnerability, as it allows any remote user to execute arbitrary commands with the highest privileges without any authentication.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard management agents require strict authentication and authorization before executing privileged actions; this code bypasses authentication entirely, violating fundamental security principles.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate management agents may execute requests as root, but only after verifying credentials and enforcing access controls.
key_indicators: Missing authentication check for privileged operations
Root-level code execution triggered directly by network input
Service listening on well-known management ports (5985, 5986, 1270)
No validation of request origin or user identity

execution_context.trigger: runtime (local UNIX socket or HTTP API request)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the OMI agent receives a local or remote request via UNIX socket or HTTP API, it processes user-supplied input, escalates privileges to root using setuid(0), and executes the input as a command, enabling unprivileged users to gain root access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing user-controlled input to be executed as root without proper validation or authentication enables attackers to escalate privileges and fully compromise the system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Privilege separation should prevent unprivileged users from executing commands as root via management APIs; this code fails to enforce such separation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: setuid(0) is used in legitimate daemons, but only after strict validation, authentication, and input sanitization.
key_indicators: Execution of user-controlled input as root
Lack of input validation or sanitization
Privilege escalation logic accessible via management API

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request to the OMI agent on an exposed management port (5985, 5986, 1270) without authentication.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution as root on the target VM

attack_chain.action: Attacker or local user sends a crafted request via UNIX socket or HTTP API to trigger privilege escalation logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation to root, enabling full system compromise

behavioral_signatures: OMI agent process (omi) accepting unauthenticated requests on ports 5985, 5986, or 1270
Unexpected root-level process execution initiated by network or local socket input to the OMI agent
Privilege escalation events involving the OMI management API, especially from unprivileged users
network_indicators: Inbound unauthenticated HTTP requests to ports 5985, 5986, or 1270
Unusual outbound connections initiated by the OMI agent process, especially following unauthenticated inbound requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for OMI agent processes (omi) listening on management ports (5985, 5986, 1270) and accepting unauthenticated requests. Alert on any root-level process execution or privilege escalation events initiated by the OMI agent in response to network or local socket input. Audit for the presence of OMI binaries and service files on systems, especially if not explicitly installed. Restrict network access to OMI ports and ensure OMI is updated to version 1.6.8-1 or later to mitigate known vulnerabilities.
